summary: python -m evals --case NAME restricts a run to named cases of one corpus, so re-measuring the few that moved does not cost the whole corpus.
details: A re-measurement asks about the cases that moved. Without this, re-drawing four participation failures at --sample 3 pays for all thirteen participation cases three times -- which is how a sample count gets chosen by budget instead of by the question, and sample_read's UNSTABLE is exactly the answer that needs draws.

Measured on the deploy host 2026-09-21: a full turn is a median of 6 model calls and ~118k input tokens (production traces, Langfuse), so corpus-sized re-runs are the dominant cost of iterating on this suite.
`--case` is repeatable and requires exactly one corpus. A name matching no ACTIVE case is refused by name rather than silently selecting zero, which would report a clean corpus.
tests/unit/test_eval_scenarios.py pins selection, its interaction with --sample, and the refusal.
